subject: C20
required_fixes: F1 (high) — crates/desktop-core/src/harness/session.rs:1023,1263,428: a refused history read leaves latest pointing to an earlier turn's export; end_turn does not invalidate it, and renewal checks only whether latest exists. After turn A exports successfully and turn B's export is refused, renewing for turn C restores A and sends C while the displayed transcript still includes B. Track export freshness against the current engine conversation, or obtain a fresh compatible export before restarting; refuse continuation without sending when current context cannot be restored. Acceptance: a production-interface test succeeds exporting A, refuses B's export, then requests renewal and proves B is either present in the restored engine context or continuation fails truthfully with no C request; no older checkpoint may silently replace current context.

F2 (high) — crates/desktop-core/src/authority/harness_identity.rs:349,724 versus authority.rs:4183,4363: initial sign-in and refresh-token rotation add a cleanup entry but never reserve writes_in_flight, and save_with accepts StoreError::Unconfirmed without the existing confirming durability step. Concurrent cleanup/reset can delete or settle that entry while Keychain.put is pending; a cancelled/stale completion can then leave an untracked item, or a successful completion can reference an item already deleted. Use the existing confirmed write-ahead/in-flight settlement contract for both paths, retaining ownership through stale completion. Acceptance: barrier-controlled initial and rotated writes interleaved with cancellation, sign-out, cleanup and reset leave no orphaned item and no committed grant pointing at a deleted item; an unconfirmed ledger that cannot be confirmed must not authorize a Keychain write.

F3 (high) — crates/desktop-core/src/authority/harness_identity.rs:327,369,755: interactive re-sign-in and renewal are not serialized under the same grant's material revision. grant_current checks only stable grant ID and subject. A renewal started with record A may finish after same-account re-sign-in installs record B, overwrite the stored pointer with C, and schedule only A for cleanup; B becomes untracked. Preserve the stable engine binding while serializing or compare-and-swapping the current credential material generation; dispose of every superseded token/record. Acceptance: hold a refresh response or rotation write, complete same-account re-sign-in, then release it in both orders; exactly the current refresh record remains owned, stale completion cannot overwrite newer material, and compatible history retains the same grant binding.

F4 (high) — crates/desktop-core/src/authority/harness_history.rs:559, crates/desktop-core/src/harness/history.rs:192,270, and authority.rs:3960-4070: protected-history placement is outside the reset/deletion fences and writer accounting. A sink already past note_history_scope can place a key/file after tenant cleanup or namespace purge. Reset also never removes adapters.harness.history_root, even with no concurrent writer. Integrate Harness saves and key creation with tenant removal/reset serialization and purge the history root, with truthful cleanup failure reporting. Acceptance: reset after saving removes the Harness records and keys; barrier-controlled saves racing tenant deletion/reset cannot recreate files or keys after successful cleanup, including after relaunch.

F5 (medium) — apps/desktop/src/features/harness/history-panel.tsx:135 and harness-view.test.tsx:432: Delete unreadable conversation immediately dispatches irreversible deletion. This bypasses D047's confirmation rule and can destroy recoverable encrypted work when its key is temporarily missing or replaced. Apply an explicit confirmation/cancel flow to unreadable records as well. Acceptance: the first activation deletes nothing, Keep it preserves the file, and only confirmation removes the selected unreadable record; cover the native keyboard/focus flow.
evidence_gaps: C20's packet describes scripted refused/unanswered history reads and refused restore as exercised failure modes, but history-refuse, history-silent and restore-refuse occur only in the stand-in implementation; none is selected by the supplied tests. The ten C20 integration tests and current native scenarios therefore do not establish those recovery/timeout assertions. Add actual production-interface exercises, retain their results, and include the stale-export sequence in F1.

The required C20 T23 offline launch/local-history read/export and reconnect-without-replay scenario is not demonstrated: C20 native relaunch keeps the synthetic services available. Scoped evidence also lacks sign-out during an in-flight Harness authorization/exchange and expiry encountered after sleep/wake. Earlier Academy offline checks and C19 stopping on sleep do not establish these new Harness identity/history behaviors. Supply deterministic scoped evidence, including cancellation/late completion and an expired credential before any resumed explicit turn.

After one successful unknown-key refresh, a second legitimate key rotation forces re-sign-in; document that limitation if retained until live qualification.
